The Arctic Ocean is nearly ice-free, and a group of homeless white bears has climbed aboard the black bears' isle. One isle cannot hold two kinds of bear. Isle of Bears is a sharp two-player abstract fought over sixteen spaces and four small isles. Each turn you play one action card: march a stack in a straight line or along a diagonal, leap it anywhere on the board, swap two spaces, gather the neighbours into a single pile, or shove an entire row until the bear at the end falls into the sea. Bears stack, and only the bear on top controls its space, so one shove can flip a whole position. Both hands are face up; nothing is hidden but the order of your deck. Crowd a space and bears drown; empty an isle and it sinks for good. Top every occupied space with your own bears to win. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Full rules and an animated card guide: isle-of-bears.heybyedesign.com/rules Isle of Bears is a two-player abstract. Summer, 2050 — the Arctic is nearly ice-free, and homeless white bears have climbed aboard the black bears' isle. One isle cannot hold two kinds of bear. Contents 1 Objective 2 Board 3 Turn sequence 4 Card effects 5 Rulings worth knowing 6 Winning 7 On BGA Objective Win the moment every occupied space is topped by bears of your colour . The bear on top of a stack controls that space, and every bear beneath it. Board 4 isles, each 2×2, making a 4×4 grid of 16 spaces. 16 bears start on the board, one per space — 8 white, 8 black. Each player has a deck of 13 action cards and a hand of 3, face up . Both hands are public information; only the deck order is hidden. Turn sequence Play one card, then resolve these steps in order: Play a card — choose one of your three face-up cards and resolve its effect. A card affects all bears on a space; a stack always moves together. Overcrowding — a space safely holds 5 bears. If any space holds 6 or more after the effect resolves, all of the opponent's bears on that space are removed from the game (they fall into the sea). Only the active player's bears stay. Sinking isles — any isle with no bears left on it sinks and is removed from play. Its spaces no longer exist. Discard & draw — the cards used this turn go to their owner's discard pile, then you draw back up to 3. If your deck runs out, reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck. Play then passes to your opponent. Card effects Each player has the same 13 cards. See the animated card guide for a before → after board for every card. Straight — Move the whole stack any distance up, down, left or right — landing on other stacks on top. Diagonal — Same idea, but along the four diagonals. Leap — Any direction, any distance — move the stack to any space on the board. Swap — Two spaces trade their entire stacks. Party — The four orthogonal neighbours all pile onto the centre; you choose the stacking order. Push — Your own bear is the pusher and moves along; all eight directions work (an empty direction is a plain one-step move), and a bear pushed off the isle falls into the sea. Dismiss — Released one at a time from the bottom up — each bear goes next to the previous one (restacking allowed), spreading out like a path. Banish — Pick a space: every bear there, including your own, goes into the sea. Play Twice — Activate other cards in front of you, two activations in total — two different cards, or the same one twice. Discard a Card — Send one of your opponent's face-up cards to their discard pile; they draw only at the end of their turn. Wild Card — Activate any face-up card from either player — Play Twice included. On an opponent's card, black and white swap. Everything used is discarded together. Rulings worth knowing "Your bears" is decided by the colour on top of a stack. When Wild Card activates an opponent's card, "your" always means the player who played the Wild Card. [Rating: 7/10] Fun but too luck dependent. The play twice action is too strong and there are very weak cards like swap.

[Rating: 7.5/10] A gorgeous 2-players game with nice production and cute artwork by the designer themselves. The game has many tactic decision with some luck of card draw built into it. But the game is quick and you can always got for another game.

[Rating: 8.25/10] Tutorial & Review: https://youtu.be/fhprPDxd5uI  This title was such a wonderful surprise! Not only is it super cute, but it's also a very tactile game that's surprisingly cutthroat and brutal!  It's another brilliant game from the designer, who also brought us the abstract game PWNED! last year. I would absolutely love to see Isle of Bears receive an international release, as I've found this to be quite an exceptional two player abstract strategy game!

[Rating: 9/10] A small game that strikes a balance between strategy and luck, but the art style is really cute.

[Rating: 10/10] Played this twice and liked it a lot. Easy to teach, quick to play, and the stacking part is really fun. Good for 2 players who want something short but smart.

[Rating: 10/10] An amazing and super-cute game. The components are fantastic, and its a super-nice game to enjoy with your significant other!

[Rating: 10/10] This is another one of those games I liked the moment I saw it — the cuteness of the bears, and the colourful, eye-catching art. I got this game at the convention in Taiwan; it was literally the first game sitting at the front of the event, and one of the games that made me decide to fly over and buy it in Taiwan. In this game you control either the white or the black bears, and it's strictly a 2-player game. Your goal is to do whatever it takes so that only your bears remain.
